summary: Build 42 Stable. Quiet in the Lua tree -- a file-level diff between 42.19 and 42.20 shows one file changing root (gamepadBinding, shared to client) and two meaningful removals (ISFarmingCursor, and the LastStand Challenge2 family). But the tree diff is not the whole story: 42.20 also narrowed getFileWriter to a whitelist of file extensions, which no file diff can surface because the change is Java-side. Any mod that writes .json from Lua breaks silently and hard. 133 of the 137 redirects Unbreaker ships were unaffected.

changes.description: B42.20 moved gamepadBinding.lua from media/lua/shared to media/lua/client. A require for it from a shared or server context now returns nil.
changes.context: The 42.20 changelog states the file was moved 'to prevent client-side bindings from being overridden on server join'. Confirmed by diffing the 42.19 vanilla Lua mirror against an installed 42.20: this is the ONLY file in the entire build that changed root. The global gamepadBinding is still set at the top level of client/gamepadBinding.lua, so client-context code is unaffected and this warning can be ignored if the requiring file is itself client-side. Unbreaker covers it from data v0.8.0 onward.

changes.description: ISFarmingCursor was deleted in B42.20. The global no longer exists and the module cannot be required.
changes.context: server/Farming/BuildingObjects/ISFarmingCursor.lua existed in 42.19 and is gone in 42.20. The changelog never mentions it; this was found by file diff. The surviving sibling ISFarmingCursorMouse is NOT a drop-in replacement, which is why no automatic redirect exists and why this rule does not name it as a replacement: both derive ISBuildingObject and share create, new, render, getAPrompt, getLBPrompt and getRBPrompt, but the deleted class also had getObjectList, isValid, onJoypadPressButton and rotateKey. Porting is a real code change, not a rename. The regex deliberately excludes ISFarmingCursorMouse so surviving code is not flagged.

changes.description: The LastStand Challenge2 module and its five ISChallenge2* UI windows were removed in B42.20 when the Challenge Modes were revamped.
changes.context: 42.20 replaced 'Cabin in the Woods' in the challenge rotation with two new modes, '28 Minutes Later' and 'Top of the World'. Removed with it: client/LastStand/Challenge2 plus ISChallenge2PlayerUpWindow, ISChallenge2UpgradeTab, ISChallenge2VariousItemWindow, ISChallenge2WeaponRepairWindow and ISChallenge2WeaponUpWindow. The replacements are client/LastStand/28MinutesLater and client/LastStand/TopOfTheWorld, which are new modes rather than renamed classes, so there is no mechanical port. Only affects challenge-mode mods.

changes.description: getFileWriter refuses to open files with certain extensions in B42.20 and returns nil instead of a writer. Writing .json, .dat or .tmp fails; .txt, .ini and .cfg still work. Calling a method on the nil result throws 'attempted index: close of non-table: null'.
changes.context: Measured directly on an installed 42.20.0 with a capability probe that varied three dimensions independently: extension, overwrite vs append (3rd arg), and root vs subdirectory of Zomboid/Lua/. Result: .txt, .ini and .cfg opened in all four combinations; .json, .dat and .tmp opened in none. The append flag and the directory make no difference, so this is purely an extension check. A control probe on a file already known to be writable (log.txt, append) returned true, ruling out the probe itself being at fault. getFileReader is NOT affected: .json files remain readable, so a mod that reads config it never writes will not notice. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMITS: only those six extensions were tested, so the full accepted set is unknown -- treat .txt/.ini/.cfg as known-good rather than as the whole whitelist. The attribution to 42.20 specifically is inferred from timeline rather than an A/B test against 42.19: the affected tool last wrote .json successfully on 2026-07-26 and 42.20 shipped 2026-07-29. The regex only catches string literals, so paths built from variables or concatenation will be missed; a mod doing its own file I/O should be checked by hand. Fix is to change the extension (contents can stay JSON) and to nil-guard the writer, since the failure mode is a nil return rather than a thrown error at the call site. Watch for double extensions too: a sentinel named 'foo.json.ready' is rejected on the .ready, not the .json.
